assertion_review: 299: assert sent == [] fails if the code signals the srun client, which is exactly the behaviour the reverted-source control restores; this is the regression guard.
301-302: the all(...) bound over attempts is vacuously true when attempts is empty, the no-record case it names; it bounds attempt timing only where inner attempts were made.

305-309: assert inner and ended == [303] for a record that appears late fails if a late record does not reopen the inner stop path; assert inner == [] and ended == [] for no record fails if the inner path runs without a record.
310-320: the closed refusal receipt set fails if a refusal is not written, carries the wrong reason or outcome, or more than one is written; line 319 names the client pid the test itself supplied.
321: assert not senders.jsonl exists fails if a refusal is written even though the record arrived before the settle window.
457-519 (probe, allocation-only): sacct state, zero signal field, delivered inner PIDs and the protected bwrap/client exclusion fail if the live stop cancels the step or signals a protected process.

findings.text: follow-on: the repair removed the pending-step client signal entirely and left no scheduler-confirmed replacement, so a genuinely pending srun --overlap request can no longer be ended by the supervisor; live plan section 3 requires that a stop still end such a run: the supervisor must ask the scheduler for the run-named step and signal the client by pid only when no such step exists. The fail-closed trade is safe and is recorded in the node's follow_ons, but the section's designed escape hatch is now unimplemented and a pending request holds its run slot while the supervisor waits.

follow-on: the receipt assertion compares entry["target_pid"] against the literal 101, which is the same pid the test hands to _reap_worker_on_its_terminal_manifest at line 287, and signal_step's assert pid == 101 at line 273 rechecks the same input; both move with the value under test and cannot catch a wrong-target defect independently, unlike the meaningful guard assert sent == [] at line 299.

follow-on: the all(...) bound over attempts at line 301 is vacuously true when attempts is empty, which is exactly the record_at is None case it is written to bound; the assertion carries no weight in the no-record case and the refusal-receipt check at line 313 is what holds there.
